thread:
support_jamie: heads up — ACME (tenant acme-147) reporting repeated 429s on their Dedicated pool since ~08:03 UTC. They say latency also spiked. Customer pasted a sample error:

customer_acme: We're getting 429s on batch endpoints after migrating to the new reserved plan. Everything worked yesterday. Can you look?

support_jamie: pasted their error snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{ "error": "rate_limited", "retry_after": 17 }
```

sre_maya: @support_jamie — can you drop tenant id and last 429 sample timestamp? also link to the dedicated pool dash (ops link preferred).

support_jamie: tenant_id=acme-147. last failing request logged at 2025-11-03T08:04:12Z. pool = ded-us-west-3a-004 (GPU util ~60%). dashboard: https://ops.redwood/dedicated/ded-us-west-3a-004

eng_infra_dev: grabbing quota config from onboarding DB for acme-147 — noticed something odd. Their plan maps to 1200 units/min but the unit type saved is `requests/min` (hosted product), while dedicated expects `tokens/min`. That mismatch would cause the runtime to apply a much lower effective token cap. Snip from DB:
```json
{
  "tenant": "acme-147",
  "plan": "pro-reserved",
  "quota": { "amount": 1200, "unit": "requests/min" }
}
```

eng_infra_dev: quick way to repro locally: call their endpoint with a multi-token prompt and watch the quota headers. Example:
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" \n  -d '{"input": "repeat token-heavy prompt..."}' \n  https://dedicated.redwood/api/v1/generate | jq .headers
```
You should see X-RateLimit-Remaining drop to 0 quickly if mapping is wrong.

ops-bot: [autoscaler] 2025-11-03T08:05:02Z scale_event: skipped scale-up for pool ded-us-west-3a-004 due to tenant_rate_cap(acme-147) enforcement.

eng_infra_dev: tl;dr — onboarding script stored hosted-style units. Dedicated runtime enforces tenant caps in token space. Because acme's numeric quota was much lower in token terms, runtime started returning 429s even though GPUs were underutilized. Noisy neighbor NOT the root cause here.

sre_maya: good find. Can we confirm by temporarily overriding acme-147 quota to tokens/min=120000 and see if errors stop? if so, roll forward with fix in onboarding mapping.

support_jamie: applied an admin override: set tenant.quota = {amount: 120000, unit: tokens/min} for acme-147 at 08:09 UTC. Customer reports errors dropped within one minute. :white_check_mark:

customer_acme: confirmed — 429s stopped after ~08:10. thanks. We had a burst job, hope billing is ok.

billing_paul: flagged — if we increase effective quota we may owe credit or bill extra usage. tagging billing team to reconcile earlier undercount.

eng_infra_dev: created PR to fix onboarding mapping and added a validation that rejects plan/unit combos that mismatch deployment mode. Patch: https://git.redwood/infra/patches/PR-3421

sre_maya: next actions: 1) revert admin override after mapping fix and test canary; 2) add e2e to onboarding tests for dedicated vs hosted unit types; 3) postmortem note and customer comms draft. I'll own the postmortem.

support_jamie: thanks everyone. Closing the incident from support side — customer happy for now. Follow-ups: ENG-3421 (onboarding mapping), OPS-445 (auto-detect unit mismatch), BILL-78 (billing reconcile).

sre_maya: closing loop — root cause = misconfigured quota unit on tenant created by legacy onboarding job. Not a noisy neighbor or autoscaler bug. Will publish short RCA later. :memo:
